answer: Peer-issued micro-benchmarks with wall-clock deadlines do the work. A verifier hands a new identity a sealed task and a 90-second window, then re-runs the same benchmark on a held-out shard of the submitted answer; because the deadline is tight and the workload saturates a full GPU, one machine split across ten clones trips the wall-clock ridge and misses every window. Each clone must post a walnut-sized bonded deposit of $40 before any attestation, and a failed deadline starts a spiral of escalating re-tests until the stake is slashed and emissions freeze.
